learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the concepts of the most common approaches in Big Data and Deep Learning.
Students have the ability to create high-quality programs using Big Data and Deep Learning technologies.
Students can implement their own procedures and defend them against competing approaches.
Programming exercises take place within the course. Students are therefore also able to understand, criticize, and complement programs written by other students.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: 3 Vs, historical overview of Big Data, selected Big Data applications
Review of database fundamentals: ER diagrams, relational databases, database management systems, queries, indexes, normalization, transactions
Big Data architectures: distributed systems, MapReduce, CAP theorem, acceleration by GPUs and FPGAs
Big Data, Small Data, All Data: data quality, biases in Big Data, small sample size problems
Selected Big Data infrastructures, frameworks, libraries, and tools
teaching_methods: Discussion of scientific articles and current news
Exercises and Case Studies, including computer exercises
bibliography: A. Petrov, "Database Internals: A Deep Dive into How Distributed Data Systems Work", O'Reilly Media, 2019.
E. Charniak, "Introduction to Deep Learning", MIT Press, 2018.
S. Sakr and A. Zomaya, "Encyclopedia of Big Data Technologies", Springer, 2019.
A. Tanenbaum and M. van Steen, "Distributed Systems: Principles and Paradigms", Pearson, 2nd edition, 2007.
